newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees lower Q1 '97 N. American output.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees lower Q1 '97 N. American output.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Thursday its North American production is forecast to be 1,039,000 units in the first quarter of 1997, a decline of about two percent from the first period of 1996.
Ford said it expects to make 639,000 trucks -- including minivans, pickup trucks and sport/utility vehicles -- and 400,000 cars in the first quarter.
In the U.S., Ford projects it will make 531,000 trucks and 315,000 cars. In Canada, Ford expects to produce 52,000 cars and 90,000 trucks. Mexican production is seen at 33,000 cars and 18,000 trucks.
In the first quarter of 1996, Ford produced 621,000 trucks and 444,000 cars for a total of 1,065,000 units.
Ford spokesman Joel Pitcoff said the lower forecast reflects the sluggish car market.
"The projection is the car industry will be lower in the first quarter than a year ago," he said.
Pitcoff said Ford's most recent fourth quarter production estimate is 1,046,000, a 1,000 unit increase from the November projection.
Last week, General Motors Corp said it expects a 16 percent increase in first quarter production to 1,413,000 units. Chrysler Corp has not publicly released its first quarter estimate.
